source.title: Minimizing the Accumulated Trajectory Error to Improve Dataset Distillation
source.authors: Jia-Wei Du; Yi-Di Jiang; Vincent Y. F. Tan; Joey Tianyi Zhou; Haizhou Li

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether a flat minimum alone improves generalization of distilled data and reports that it does not; it also reports that a flatter teacher trajectory reduces accumulated trajectory error and improves test accuracy. This is a refinement of the claim's generalization-measure account, not a direct test of most listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies dataset distillation and test accuracy, rather than the claim's natural-label versus random-label memorization comparison or most mapped conditions. Rows capture the paper's own trajectory-error and flat-minimum experiments. Baseline comparisons cited from prior work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses sharpness-aware training to improve dataset distillation. Its flat-minimum ablation measures test accuracy after SAM training, not whether magnitude-aware sharpness ranks training–test gaps among networks with similarly low training loss. Neither this ablation nor the trajectory-error results test V7 or another listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute FTD's improved dataset-distillation performance primarily to reduced accumulated trajectory error from flatter teacher trajectories. Their SAM ablation finds that seeking a flat terminal minimum alone does not explain the improvement.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses trajectory-matching dataset distillation and adds flat-trajectory regularization to teacher training; it does not test the original claim's random-label memorization setup or its specified interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, images per class, and training phase affect the reported dataset-distillation outcomes. The flat-minimum comparison tests several ρ values, but exact accuracies are available only in a figure.

fits_no_version.finding: Applying SAM at several perturbation radii during training on MTT synthetic data does not improve generalization according to Section 4.3 and Figure 4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Seeking a flat terminal minimum with SAM alone need not improve real-test accuracy when training on distilled synthetic data.

fits_no_version.finding: MTT's student–teacher test-loss difference accumulates during evaluation; FTD has a lower difference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularizing teacher trajectories for flatness can reduce accumulated trajectory error in dataset distillation.

record.problems: The flat-minimum comparison is reported only in a plot, with no exact values in the text. Evaluation uses five random initializations per synthetic set, reported as mean accuracy and standard deviation; the paper's trajectory-error figure gives no numeric values in text.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible outcomes were omitted. Results in Tables 1–5 primarily concern distilled-set accuracy, cross-architecture performance, and architecture-search rank correlation, not a version's named behavior or measure.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.

Magnitude-aware sharpness versus training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, including comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings. An intervention intended to flatten minima does not test this correlational claim.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The synthetic-data ablation does not contradict V7's specified correlation. The paper's theoretical discussion of synthetic-data generalization bounds likewise does not establish that magnitude-aware sharpness fails to rank observed generalization gaps.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
It tests whether flat minima improve generalization of synthetic data, but does not test the specified magnitude-aware sharpness measure or rank it against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: MTT + Flat Minimum
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the synthetic dataset using SAM to bias convergence toward a flat minimum; evaluated across tested ρ values.
rows.note: Authors state that a flatter minimum does not help the synthetic dataset generalize well; exact plotted values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Remove the V7 link. Section 4.3 reports no accuracy benefit from applying SAM to MTT synthetic-data training, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness, comparable training losses, or training–test gaps. The stated absence concerns an intervention's accuracy benefit, not V7's correlation. Exact accuracies cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: MTT
rows.operation_detail: Measured loss difference between student and teacher trajectories as evaluation proceeds.
rows.note: Text says MTT's evaluation-phase loss difference accumulates and is much higher than in distillation; this is an accumulated trajectory error result, not a direct measurement of the specified V7 measure.
rows.check: This measures the difference between student and teacher test losses, not a training–test generalization gap or any listed version. Appendix A.1 identifies the distillation-phase MTT loss difference as the baseline, so 'baseline not stated' is incorrect. Retain only as a finding outside the versions.

rows.subject: FTD
rows.operation_detail: Measured loss difference between student and teacher trajectories as evaluation proceeds.
rows.note: Authors state FTD's loss difference is much lower than MTT's, indicating reduced accumulated trajectory error.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's trajectory-matching performance relative to MTT. Lower student–teacher test-loss difference cannot establish any listed version; the assigned 'partial' state has no claim-linked interpretation. Retain only as a finding outside the versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
